items.title: Continuous Improvement In TA
bullets: Tony de Graaf ranks every possible TA improvement by one test: what has the biggest impact on consistently delivering the right person exactly on time.
Before buying a narrow AI tool, explain how its time saving beats the setup and processing time it adds, or de Graaf says it is not time to implement it.
The job intake meeting was the weakest point in last year's Recruiting Excellence Foundation benchmark, and de Graaf says technology does not fix it.
items.guest_line: Tony de Graaf · Co-Founder @ Recruiting Excellence Foundation

items.title: Grok Bot for Recruiters
bullets: Joe Atkinson keeps the facts his recruiting agent works from in his own tools, such as Airtable, rather than in the agent's memory.
Atkinson's standing instruction to his agent is to take no action unless he says otherwise, and to check with him first.
To find sales overachievers, Jason Miller builds out synonyms for overattainment in his searches, such as president's club or 200% attainment.

items.section: Recruiting reports, product updates, and more
items.title: Staffing Industry Indicator, week ending 24 October 2026
bullets: US staffing hours rose 11% year over year in the week ended 24 October 2026, according to the SIA and Bullhorn Staffing Indicator.
In the week ended 24 October, US industrial staffing hours advanced 17% year over year while US office and clerical hours fell 7%.
SIA says the US industrial staffing indicator is now higher than it was at this time of year one, two and three years ago.
items.check_note: Partial extraction: public SIA news summary only. Verify against the URL.

items.title: Why PMs are suddenly valuable again
bullets: Gemini product head Tulsee Doshi says a first eval, a set of test prompts for checking an AI's answers, can start with just five prompts and your own judgement.
When hiring product managers to work on AI models, Doshi wants people with opinions formed from using models daily, who can build an eval themselves.
Doshi's test for handing work to AI: if you have to do something twice, ask whether you need to do it yourself.
items.guest_line: Tulsee Doshi · Head of Product, Gemini @ Google

items.title: AI is speeding up recruitment, and putting agency fees under pressure
bullets: In a 2026 Bullhorn survey of nearly 300 UK and Irish recruitment professionals, 37% said AI made candidate screening 26% to 50% faster.
David Berwick of Adria Solutions says AI is making an agency that simply forwards CVs increasingly difficult to justify.
Matt Collingwood of VIQU Group sees every reason for agency fees to hold firm or even increase, if the value agencies deliver keeps growing.

preview_changed.text: UK vacancies have fallen to their lowest outside the pandemic since 2014, and REC finds UK employers' permanent hiring intentions edging down. Talent engineering is the argument of the week, from a Zapier talent engineer's case for buying over building to Data Driven Recruiter asking whether the job is real. Pin and Teamtailor ship AI that acts on candidates, Dayforce is buying AI interviewing firm Ribbon AI, and UK agency recruiters are split on whether AI will push their fees down. And in the world of AI, a Figma product manager runs his day from shared AI skills, and Kevin Roose had Claude agents review his book.
